match.reason: The bank point 'Stalin's Soviet Union' covers only Stalin's personal dictatorship, while the new point covers Lenin and Stalin together, one-party rule, state ownership of industry and farms, and terror, so it is narrower than the brief and would need new content rather than small changes.

rejected.title: Communism in the Soviet Union
card: One-party rule
After the 1917 revolution, the Communist Party ruled alone under Lenin. Other parties were banned, and there were no free elections.
State ownership
The state owned industry and, under Stalin, took over farms. Farmers were forced into collective farms, and the economy ran on state plans.
Terror
The secret police, labour camps and show trials were used against opponents. Under Stalin, the Great Terror of the late 1930s killed or jailed millions.
Stalin
After Lenin died in 1924, Stalin won the power struggle and became the leader with the most power.
rejected.remember: Soviet communism meant one party, state ownership and terror against opponents.

a.q: What did Stalin's collectivisation do to Soviet farming?
opts: Farms were taken from private owners and run collectively
Farmers were given larger plots to run for profit
Farms were handed to local elected councils
Farm owners were paid to sell land to the state
a.why: Collectivisation moved farmland out of private hands into collective farms under state control. Private profit and elected control did not fit one-party state ownership, which is why those options are wrong.

b.q: In 1937 a Soviet official is arrested after a short show trial and sent to a labour camp. What does this show about Stalin's rule?
opts: Opponents were removed through terror
Courts could rule against the government
Opposition parties were allowed to compete
Officials were chosen by free elections
b.why: Show trials and labour camps were tools of terror used to remove opponents. A trial staged to reach a set result is not independent, so it does not show courts that could rule against the government.
b.clue: Was the trial a real test of guilt?

version.title: Communism in the Soviet Union
card: One-party rule
after the Bolsheviks seized power in 1917, Lenin's Communist Party ruled alone. Other parties were banned, and elections offered no real choice.
Stalin
after Lenin died in 1924, Stalin outmanoeuvred his rivals in the party. By the late 1920s he held supreme power.
State control
the state took over large industry, and from 1928 Stalin's five-year plans set what factories made. Collectivisation forced peasants onto collective farms run under state control.
Terror
the secret police, show trials and labour camps known as the Gulag were used against opponents. In the Great Terror of 1936 to 1938, hundreds of thousands were executed.
version.remember: Soviet communism meant one party, state control of the economy and terror against opponents.

a.q: What did collectivisation change about farming in the Soviet Union?
opts: Private farms were merged into state-controlled farms
Peasants were given bigger plots to farm for profit
Farms were handed to councils chosen in free votes
Landowners were paid a fair price to sell to the state
a.why: Collectivisation took farmland out of private hands and forced peasants onto collective farms under state control. Farming for private profit was the opposite of what Stalin wanted.

b.q: In 1937 a factory manager in Leningrad is arrested by the secret police, confesses at a staged trial and is sent to a labour camp. What does this show about Stalin's rule?
opts: Terror was used to remove possible opponents
Courts were free to rule against the state
Rival parties could still compete for power
Managers were chosen through free elections
b.why: Arrests by the secret police, staged trials and labour camps were tools of terror. A trial with its result decided beforehand shows that courts were not free to rule against the state.
b.clue: Was the trial a real test of guilt?

a.best: Private farms were merged into state-controlled farms

b.best: Terror was used to remove possible opponents
